import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io

# Load the dataset from the string
csv_data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Data Cleaning and Preparation
# Fill NaN in 'Sleep Disorder' with 'None' for clarity in plotting
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Split 'Blood Pressure' into 'Systolic' and 'Diastolic' columns
df[['Systolic', 'Diastolic']] = df['Blood Pressure'].str.split('/', expand=True)
df['Systolic'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Systolic'])
df['Diastolic'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Diastolic'])

# Set up the visualization style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.set_context("talk")

# Create a 2x2 subplot grid for a comprehensive dashboard view
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(18, 14))
fig.suptitle('Comprehensive Health and Sleep Analysis', fontsize=24, weight='bold')

# --- Plot 1: Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep ---
# Color-coded by Sleep Disorder to see if there's a pattern
sns.scatterplot(
    ax=axes[0, 0],
    data=df,
    x='Quality of Sleep',
    y='Sleep Duration',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    size='Stress Level',
    sizes=(100, 400),
    palette='viridis',
    edgecolor='black',
    alpha=0.8
)
axes[0, 0].set_title('Sleep Quality vs. Duration by Disorder', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)')
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)')
axes[0, 0].legend(title='Sleep Disorder & Stress')


# --- Plot 2: Stress Level Distribution by Occupation ---
# A boxenplot provides more detail about the distribution shape than a standard boxplot
sns.boxenplot(
    ax=axes[0, 1],
    data=df,
    x='Stress Level',
    y='Occupation',
    palette='magma'
)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Stress Levels Across Occupations', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Stress Level (1-10)')
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Occupation')


# --- Plot 3: Physical Activity vs. Heart Rate ---
# Using a regression plot to show the trend, colored by BMI Category
sns.lmplot(
    data=df,
    x='Daily Steps',
    y='Heart Rate',
    hue='BMI Category',
    height=6,
    aspect=1.3,
    palette='plasma',
    legend=False # We will use the subplot axis instead
)
# This lmplot creates its own figure, so we'll "re-draw" it onto our axis for a unified layout.
# A simpler approach for subplots is to use regplot.
sns.regplot(
    ax=axes[1, 0],
    data=df[df['BMI Category'] == 'Normal'],
    x='Daily Steps',
    y='Heart Rate',
    color=sns.color_palette('plasma', 3)[0],
    label='Normal',
    scatter_kws={'s': 150, 'edgecolor':'w'}
)
sns.regplot(
    ax=axes[1, 0],
    data=df[df['BMI Category'] == 'Overweight'],
    x='Daily Steps',
    y='Heart Rate',
    color=sns.color_palette('plasma', 3)[1],
    label='Overweight',
    scatter_kws={'s': 150, 'edgecolor':'w'}
)
sns.regplot(
    ax=axes[1, 0],
    data=df[df['BMI Category'] == 'Obese'],
    x='Daily Steps',
    y='Heart Rate',
    color=sns.color_palette('plasma', 3)[2],
    label='Obese',
    scatter_kws={'s': 150, 'edgecolor':'w'}
)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Daily Steps vs. Heart Rate by BMI', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Daily Steps')
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Resting Heart Rate (bpm)')
axes[1, 0].legend(title='BMI Category')


# --- Plot 4: Blood Pressure by Sleep Disorder ---
# A violin plot to show the distribution of systolic blood pressure
sns.violinplot(
    ax=axes[1, 1],
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Disorder',
    y='Systolic',
    palette='coolwarm',
    inner='quartile'
)
sns.stripplot(
    ax=axes[1, 1],
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Disorder',
    y='Systolic',
    color='black',
    alpha=0.7,
    jitter=0.1
)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Systolic Blood Pressure Distribution', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Sleep Disorder')
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Systolic Blood Pressure (mmHg)')
axes[1, 1].axhline(120, color='grey', linestyle='--', linewidth=2)
axes[1, 1].text(1.5, 121, 'Normal Threshold (120)', color='grey', ha='center')

# Adjust layout to prevent overlap and save the figure
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
